corrections: Replaced the generic regional aircraft with measured ATR 72-600 nose, cabin and tail stations, high-wing planform, narrow T-tail, belly sponsons, short dual-wheel main gear and six-blade PW127M nacelles.

Authored real cockpit and passenger-window apertures, asymmetric service/cargo-door outlines, seams, rivet courses, pitots, wipers, navigation lights, black de-icing boots and original geometric identification lettering.

Rebuilt the five portrait-display Thales panel against the ATR training poster; added raised AFCS glareshield, standby attitude, paired control columns, rudder pedals, dual FMS keyboards, power/condition/flap levers, side shelves and four-column overhead.
Added a 72-seat cabin with 29-inch row pitch, paired seats, overhead bins and forward baggage partition, following the 2020 manufacturer plan.

Visual corrections include top-view orientation, full-width panel camera, physical joining of the unfolded poster components, reduced excess windshield framing, airfoil-following de-icing boots and red overhead fire handles.
reviewNotes.visual: Personally inspected all four current overlays, eight standard renders and twelve detail/state captures after final corrections. Compared exterior contours, wing/tail planforms, engine/gear stations and main-panel layout against manufacturer drawings and photos. Inspected zero, cruise, limits, below-sea-level and missing telemetry; positive/negative controls, gear-up, overhead, pedestal, close exterior and passenger cabin.
limitations: Manufacturer marketing drawings contain small discrepancies between views; printed dimensions take priority. Overlays use uniform scales and recorded rigid rotations, without nonuniform fitting. Fine surface/rivet detail is representative rather than an airframe production drawing.
The 2015 drawing shows a 70-seat cabin; this model uses the later 2020 manufacturer 72-seat plan. Operator furnishings, avionics options and exact serial-number equipment are not represented.

The cockpit poster is an unfolded projection. Panel width, depth, mounting angles and pilot viewpoint are estimates checked against the manufacturer photograph and shell volume, not surveyed ergonomic measurements. Small switch labels and overhead circuitry are simplified.

Working indications use simulated true airspeed in knots, geometric altitude in feet, true heading, pitch/roll, vertical speed, flap position, gear position and independent normalized engine RPM percentages. IAS, barometric altitude, magnetic variation, air-data errors and propeller governor dynamics are not simulated.

Torque, ITT, NH, fuel, oil, electrical/hydraulic/pressurization systems, clocks, radios, navigation, FMS and AFCS lack simulation telemetry and remain blank or explicitly unavailable. The overhead, condition levers and trim controls are static. Power levers follow the shared throttle input.

Retracting gear and moving controls follow simulation state, with simplified linkages and travel. No operational cockpit-system fidelity is claimed. No source photograph or diagram pixels are embedded in the model or redistributed.

cockpitPass.problem: Eye jammed into the roof corner; the nose in plan ran 0.25 to 0.3 m too narrow forward of the barrel, so it looked long and sharp; the panel was built 1.5 times oversize and stood high in a diamond-shaped opening, with a dark hood poking through the glazing and hanging off the nose.
corrections: Nose stations and window band re-traced from the 2015 manufacturer side and plan outlines. The nose is now a smooth 40-column surface with true apertures: level sill, level header, three panes per side, dark surround, as in the S2-STF photograph.

Panel, coaming and all instruments scaled by 0.67 about their own layout (6 x 8 in displays), moved to z 11.68 and lowered. Hood replaced by one flat deck meeting the skin below the glass; blanking panels close the nose bay. Bindings and node names unchanged.

Flight deck moved 0.22 m forward and the eye lowered 0.26 m. Seats, yokes, pedals, pedestal, FMS, side shelves and overhead re-placed around it. Added a flight deck floor and a door bulkhead at the plan's 3.4 m from the nose.
cockpitPass.visual: Inspected the runtime seat view (dead ahead, 60 degrees vertical), look-down, look-right and an aisle view, plus exterior front, both quarters, low and side, after the final rebuild. Rays fanned from above over the nose hit only skin, glass and exterior frames.
cockpitPass.assumptions: Eye height is taken at mid-window from the drawing, and z from the pilot's head in the S2-STF photograph after allowing for parallax. The 1.78 m flight deck floor is inferred from that eye and normal seat geometry; no published floor height or ATR eye position was found.

limitations: Manufacturer marketing drawings contain small discrepancies between views; printed dimensions take priority. Overlays use uniform scales and recorded rigid rotations, without nonuniform fitting. Fine surface/rivet detail is representative rather than an airframe production drawing.
The 2015 drawing shows a 70-seat cabin; this model uses the later 2020 manufacturer 72-seat plan. Operator furnishings, avionics options and exact serial-number equipment are not represented.

Working indications use simulated true airspeed in knots, geometric altitude in feet, true heading, pitch/roll, vertical speed, flap position, gear position and independent normalized engine RPM percentages. IAS, barometric altitude, magnetic variation, air-data errors and propeller governor dynamics are not simulated.

Retracting gear and moving controls follow simulation state, with simplified linkages and travel. No operational cockpit-system fidelity is claimed. No source photograph or diagram pixels are embedded in the model or redistributed.

Flight deck stations (eye, 1.78 m floor, panel z) are reconstructed from drawings and photographs; ATR's published design eye and cut-off angle were not found. The windscreen panes are gently curved on the skin rather than the real flat panes, the side sliding window has no handle or frame detail, and the cockpit walls are bare skin with no liner, sun visors or standby compass.
